% Abstract: Structural stagnation detection in LLM coding agents (EMNLP 2026 ARR)
LLM-based agents deployed on software engineering tasks frequently exhibit semantic stagnation---executing diverse yet collectively unproductive action sequences that evade repetition detectors and overwhelm LLM-based judges. No systematic study has investigated what signals carry stagnation information or whether detection requires semantic understanding.

We address this gap through a systematic empirical study using a weak supervision pipeline (3 labeling functions + majority vote) over 205K+ windows from two architecturally distinct SE agents, SWE-Agent and OpenHands. We compare 30 hand-crafted structural features, a GRU-based neural embedding probe, and an LLM-as-judge baseline.

Our central finding is that stagnation signals are fundamentally structural: 30 features---command repetition rates, file operation counts, edit distances---achieve RF 0.9951 in-domain and GB 0.9674 cross-agent macro-F1, surpassing the neural probe (0.9055) and LLM-as-judge (0.6625) by wide margins. In-domain evaluation reflects circular agreement with LF-derived silver labels; cross-agent transfer and a pending gold set provide non-circular validation. Structural features are also extremely data-efficient, achieving $>$0.987 macro-F1 at just 10\% training data.

Analysis of labeling function temporal dynamics reveals agent-specific roles: command repetition leads stagnation by 1.87 steps on SWE-Agent but reverses on OpenHands, where removing it improves fine-tuned F1 by 17.6 percentage points. Labeling functions validated on one agent can become adversarial on another.

Despite these well-characterized temporal patterns, three temporal label models (time-varying weights, HMM, lag-aware HMM) fail to improve over majority vote---a negative result we attribute to insufficient inter-LF conflict in the 3-function regime.

1	\section{Introduction}
2	\label{sec:introduction}
3	
4	LLM agents are increasingly deployed for complex, long-horizon software engineering tasks---resolving GitHub issues, debugging production systems, and iterating on multi-file codebases across dozens of editing rounds \citep{jimenez2024swebench,yang2024sweagent,wang2025openhands}.
5	As these deployments scale, a critical failure mode has emerged that is qualitatively different from crashes or syntax errors: the agent \emph{stagnates}---continuing to produce actions that appear purposeful while making no meaningful progress toward the task goal.
6	\citet{orlanski2026slopcodebench} document this degradation on SlopCodeBench, recording verbosity increases of 90\% and quality drops of 80\% in long-horizon coding trajectories, with no agent fully solving any benchmark problem end-to-end.
7	Crucially, the dominant failure pattern is not simple repetition but what we term \emph{semantic stagnation}: the agent issues varied commands, edits different files, and generates plausible-looking outputs, yet its behavior is functionally stuck.
8	This ``looks busy but going in circles'' pattern defeats existing monitoring tools, because surface-level action diversity masks the underlying lack of progress.
9	We observe this phenomenon at scale: across trajectories from two architecturally distinct agents---SWE-Agent \citep{yang2024sweagent} and OpenHands \citep{wang2025openhands}---on SWE-bench tasks \citep{jimenez2024swebench}, 28.5\% and 6.6\% of sliding windows exhibit stagnation under our silver labeling scheme, respectively, confirming that the failure mode is both prevalent and highly agent-dependent.
10	
11	Existing approaches address aspects of this problem but fall short in three ways.
12	First, \emph{repetition detectors} such as cycle detection \citep{george2025cycledetection} and SpecRA \citep{pipis2025reasoningloop} identify structural repetition---exact or near-exact loops in action sequences---but by design miss semantically diverse stagnation where the agent varies its surface behavior while remaining functionally stuck.
13	Second, \emph{step-level scoring} via process reward models \citep{xi2025agentprm} evaluates individual actions in isolation, discarding the window-level temporal dynamics that distinguish transient setbacks from sustained stagnation---a distinction that requires reasoning over sequences of consecutive actions \citep{chen2025monitoring}.
14	A sequence of failed commands followed by a strategy switch, for instance, carries different diagnostic information than the same commands evaluated independently.
15	Third, \emph{LLM self-evaluation} \citep{shinn2023reflexion} is both expensive and fundamentally limited by the stuck model's own judgment; our LLM-as-judge baseline achieves only 0.6625 macro-F1 at \$11.66 per test set, well below lightweight feature-based alternatives.
16	More fundamentally, none of these approaches asks the prior question: \emph{what signals actually carry stagnation information?}
17	No systematic study has investigated whether detecting subtle agent failure requires sophisticated semantic understanding or whether simpler structural patterns suffice.
18	
19	We address this question through a systematic empirical study (Figure~\ref{fig:pipeline}).
20	Using a weak supervision framework \citep{ratner2016dataprogramming,ratner2017snorkel}, we construct silver-labeled datasets from over 205K windows spanning SWE-Agent (54,809 windows, 28.5\% silver-labeled stagnation) and OpenHands (150,652 windows, 6.6\% stagnation).
21	Three labeling functions provide complementary noisy votes: command repetition ($\lambda_1$) targets repetitive behavior, file diff delta ($\lambda_2$) targets output productivity, and outcome backpropagation ($\lambda_3$) propagates task-level outcomes backward through the trajectory.
22	Majority vote aggregation produces window-level binary labels with confidence scores.
23	Our window-level formulation ($k{=}5$ consecutive actions, stride 1) captures short-range temporal patterns---such as repeated failures followed by strategy changes---that step-level approaches cannot express, while providing the granularity to pinpoint \emph{when} stagnation begins and ends within a trajectory, enabling targeted interventions.
24	Against these silver labels, we systematically compare hand-crafted structural features, a neural embedding probe, and an LLM-as-judge baseline.
25	
26	Our study yields three principal findings.
27	
28	\textbf{Finding 1: Stagnation signals are fundamentally structural.}
29	Thirty hand-crafted features---command repetition rates, file operation counts, edit distances---achieve 0.9951 macro-F1 in-domain (Random Forest) and 0.9674 cross-agent macro-F1 (Gradient Boosting, SWE-Agent $\to$ OpenHands), surpassing the GRU embedding probe \citep{cho2014gru} (0.9055 in-domain, 0.751 after full fine-tuning on the target agent) and the LLM-as-judge baseline (0.6625) by wide margins---up to 33.3 percentage points (pp).
30	We note that in-domain evaluation uses silver labels (\S\ref{sec:circular}); cross-agent transfer and a pending gold set (\S\ref{sec:gold_set}) provide non-circular validation.
31	The structural advantage is encoder-agnostic: three embedding backbones \citep{zhang2025qwen3embedding} all yield probe F1 above 0.90, confirming that the probe's temporal architecture rather than a specific pretrained encoder drives performance.
32	The in-domain score of 0.9951 reflects circular evaluation---structural features overlap with LF inputs---but the cross-agent score of 0.9674, where models trained on one agent's LF distribution are tested on another with substantially different firing patterns, breaks this circularity.
33	This finding challenges the prevailing intuition that detecting subtle agent failures requires complex language understanding, and suggests that lightweight structural monitoring---no GPU, under 5\,ms per window---may be more practical than neural or LLM-based approaches for real-time agent oversight.
34	
35	\textbf{Finding 2: Labeling functions occupy agent-specific temporal niches.}
36	On SWE-Agent, command repetition ($\lambda_1$) leads stagnation onset by 1.87 steps, file diff ($\lambda_2$) is near-concurrent at $-1.20$ steps, and outcome backpropagation ($\lambda_3$) lags by 6.70 steps.
37	On OpenHands, $\lambda_1$ reverses from leading to lagging ($+3.32$ steps), where its 92.2\% stagnation-vote rate produces a 71\% false positive rate on progress windows.
38	Removing $\lambda_1$ from the OpenHands labeling pipeline improves fine-tuned probe F1 by 17.6\,pp, demonstrating that labeling functions validated on one agent architecture can become adversarial on another.
39	
40	\textbf{Finding 3: Temporal label models fail to improve over majority vote.}
41	Three temporal label models---time-varying weights (TWV), Hidden Markov Models \citep{safranchik2020linkedhmm}, and lag-aware HMMs---all fail to surpass majority vote on downstream detection.
42	TWV achieves marginally higher self-evaluated F1 but degrades downstream probe performance by 2.57\,pp.
43	The root cause: three binary LFs produce too little inter-LF conflict for temporal aggregation to exploit.
44	
45	Our contributions are:
46	\begin{enumerate}
47	    \item \textbf{Structural signal discovery.} We demonstrate that 30 lightweight structural features achieve near-perfect stagnation detection (0.9951 in-domain, 0.967 cross-agent macro-F1), outperforming neural probes and LLM judges by wide margins (+33.3\,pp over LLM-as-judge), with no GPU and under 5\,ms per window. This redirects agent monitoring from costly representation learning toward lightweight structural approaches.
48	    \item \textbf{Labeling function temporal dynamics.} We reveal that labeling functions occupy statistically distinct temporal niches relative to stagnation onset, with agent-specific reversals that corrupt silver labels when transferred across architectures, informing future weak-supervision design on sequential agent data.
49	    \item \textbf{Temporal label model negative finding.} We show that three temporal label models fail to improve over majority vote for downstream detection, despite clear temporal structure in LF firing patterns. This constrains future temporal label model research: the 3-LF regime produces insufficient conflict for temporal aggregation to add value.
50	\end{enumerate}

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

LLM agents are increasingly deployed for complex, long-horizon software engineering tasks---resolving GitHub issues, debugging production systems, and iterating on multi-file codebases across dozens of editing rounds \citep{jimenez2024swebench,yang2024sweagent,wang2025openhands}.
As these deployments scale, a critical failure mode has emerged that is qualitatively different from crashes or syntax errors: the agent \emph{stagnates}---continuing to produce actions that appear purposeful while making no meaningful progress toward the task goal.
\citet{orlanski2026slopcodebench} document this degradation on SlopCodeBench, recording verbosity increases of 90\% and quality drops of 80\% in long-horizon coding trajectories, with no agent fully solving any benchmark problem end-to-end.
Crucially, the dominant failure pattern is not simple repetition but what we term \emph{semantic stagnation}: the agent issues varied commands, edits different files, and generates plausible-looking outputs, yet its behavior is functionally stuck.
This ``looks busy but going in circles'' pattern defeats existing monitoring tools, because surface-level action diversity masks the underlying lack of progress.
We observe this phenomenon at scale: across trajectories from two architecturally distinct agents---SWE-Agent \citep{yang2024sweagent} and OpenHands \citep{wang2025openhands}---on SWE-bench tasks \citep{jimenez2024swebench}, 28.5\% and 6.6\% of sliding windows exhibit stagnation under our silver labeling scheme, respectively, confirming that the failure mode is both prevalent and highly agent-dependent.

Existing approaches address aspects of this problem but fall short in three ways.
First, \emph{repetition detectors} such as cycle detection \citep{george2025cycledetection} and SpecRA \citep{pipis2025reasoningloop} identify structural repetition---exact or near-exact loops in action sequences---but by design miss semantically diverse stagnation where the agent varies its surface behavior while remaining functionally stuck.
Second, \emph{step-level scoring} via process reward models \citep{xi2025agentprm} evaluates individual actions in isolation, discarding the window-level temporal dynamics that distinguish transient setbacks from sustained stagnation---a distinction that requires reasoning over sequences of consecutive actions \citep{chen2025monitoring}.
A sequence of failed commands followed by a strategy switch, for instance, carries different diagnostic information than the same commands evaluated independently.
Third, \emph{LLM self-evaluation} \citep{shinn2023reflexion} is both expensive and fundamentally limited by the stuck model's own judgment; our LLM-as-judge baseline achieves only 0.6625 macro-F1 at \$11.66 per test set, well below lightweight feature-based alternatives.
More fundamentally, none of these approaches asks the prior question: \emph{what signals actually carry stagnation information?}
No systematic study has investigated whether detecting subtle agent failure requires sophisticated semantic understanding or whether simpler structural patterns suffice.

We address this question through a systematic empirical study (Figure~\ref{fig:pipeline}).
Using a weak supervision framework \citep{ratner2016dataprogramming,ratner2017snorkel}, we construct silver-labeled datasets from over 205K windows spanning SWE-Agent (54,809 windows, 28.5\% silver-labeled stagnation) and OpenHands (150,652 windows, 6.6\% stagnation).
Three labeling functions provide complementary noisy votes: command repetition ($\lambda_1$) targets repetitive behavior, file diff delta ($\lambda_2$) targets output productivity, and outcome backpropagation ($\lambda_3$) propagates task-level outcomes backward through the trajectory.
Majority vote aggregation produces window-level binary labels with confidence scores.
Our window-level formulation ($k{=}5$ consecutive actions, stride 1) captures short-range temporal patterns---such as repeated failures followed by strategy changes---that step-level approaches cannot express, while providing the granularity to pinpoint \emph{when} stagnation begins and ends within a trajectory, enabling targeted interventions.
Against these silver labels, we systematically compare hand-crafted structural features, a neural embedding probe, and an LLM-as-judge baseline.

Our study yields three principal findings.

\textbf{Finding 1: Stagnation signals are fundamentally structural.}
Thirty hand-crafted features---command repetition rates, file operation counts, edit distances---achieve 0.9951 macro-F1 in-domain (Random Forest) and 0.9674 cross-agent macro-F1 (Gradient Boosting, SWE-Agent $\to$ OpenHands), surpassing the GRU embedding probe \citep{cho2014gru} (0.9055 in-domain, 0.751 after full fine-tuning on the target agent) and the LLM-as-judge baseline (0.6625) by wide margins---up to 33.3 percentage points (pp).
We note that in-domain evaluation uses silver labels (\S\ref{sec:circular}); cross-agent transfer and a pending gold set (\S\ref{sec:gold_set}) provide non-circular validation.
The structural advantage is encoder-agnostic: three embedding backbones \citep{zhang2025qwen3embedding} all yield probe F1 above 0.90, confirming that the probe's temporal architecture rather than a specific pretrained encoder drives performance.
The in-domain score of 0.9951 reflects circular evaluation---structural features overlap with LF inputs---but the cross-agent score of 0.9674, where models trained on one agent's LF distribution are tested on another with substantially different firing patterns, breaks this circularity.
This finding challenges the prevailing intuition that detecting subtle agent failures requires complex language understanding, and suggests that lightweight structural monitoring---no GPU, under 5\,ms per window---may be more practical than neural or LLM-based approaches for real-time agent oversight.

\textbf{Finding 2: Labeling functions occupy agent-specific temporal niches.}
On SWE-Agent, command repetition ($\lambda_1$) leads stagnation onset by 1.87 steps, file diff ($\lambda_2$) is near-concurrent at $-1.20$ steps, and outcome backpropagation ($\lambda_3$) lags by 6.70 steps.
On OpenHands, $\lambda_1$ reverses from leading to lagging ($+3.32$ steps), where its 92.2\% stagnation-vote rate produces a 71\% false positive rate on progress windows.
Removing $\lambda_1$ from the OpenHands labeling pipeline improves fine-tuned probe F1 by 17.6\,pp, demonstrating that labeling functions validated on one agent architecture can become adversarial on another.

\textbf{Finding 3: Temporal label models fail to improve over majority vote.}
Three temporal label models---time-varying weights (TWV), Hidden Markov Models \citep{safranchik2020linkedhmm}, and lag-aware HMMs---all fail to surpass majority vote on downstream detection.
TWV achieves marginally higher self-evaluated F1 but degrades downstream probe performance by 2.57\,pp.
The root cause: three binary LFs produce too little inter-LF conflict for temporal aggregation to exploit.

Our contributions are:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{Structural signal discovery.} We demonstrate that 30 lightweight structural features achieve near-perfect stagnation detection (0.9951 in-domain, 0.967 cross-agent macro-F1), outperforming neural probes and LLM judges by wide margins (+33.3\,pp over LLM-as-judge), with no GPU and under 5\,ms per window. This redirects agent monitoring from costly representation learning toward lightweight structural approaches.
    \item \textbf{Labeling function temporal dynamics.} We reveal that labeling functions occupy statistically distinct temporal niches relative to stagnation onset, with agent-specific reversals that corrupt silver labels when transferred across architectures, informing future weak-supervision design on sequential agent data.
    \item \textbf{Temporal label model negative finding.} We show that three temporal label models fail to improve over majority vote for downstream detection, despite clear temporal structure in LF firing patterns. This constrains future temporal label model research: the 3-LF regime produces insufficient conflict for temporal aggregation to add value.
\end{enumerate}

1	\section{Experiments}
2	\label{sec:experiments}
3	
4	We evaluate stagnation detection across four axes: in-domain accuracy, cross-agent transfer, robustness to design choices, and temporal dynamics of labeling functions.
5	All reported metrics are evaluated against silver labels derived from majority vote over three labeling functions (\S\ref{sec:method}).
6	
7	\paragraph{Circular evaluation caveat.}
8	Structural features (command repetition ratios, file operation counts, edit distances) are computed from the same signals that the labeling functions use to produce silver labels.
9	Consequently, the in-domain structural F1 of 0.9951 reflects an upper bound on how well these features can \emph{reverse-engineer} the labeling functions, not detection accuracy against true ground truth.
10	The cross-agent evaluation on OpenHands (0.967 macro-F1) is non-circular: models trained on SWE-Agent LF distributions are tested on a different agent whose LF firing patterns differ substantially (\S\ref{sec:cmd_rep_ablation}).
11	A human-annotated gold set provides the definitive non-circular evaluation (\S\ref{sec:gold_set}).
12	
13	%-------------------------------------------------------------------
14	\subsection{Experimental Setup}
15	\label{sec:setup}
16	
17	\paragraph{Datasets.}
18	We extract sliding windows of $k{=}5$ consecutive actions from agent trajectories.
19	\textbf{SWE-Agent} trajectories from SWE-bench \citep{jimenez2024swebench,yang2024sweagent} yield 54,809 windows with a stagnation ratio of 28.5\%.
20	\textbf{OpenHands} (OH) trajectories \citep{wang2025openhands} yield 150,652 windows with a stagnation ratio of 6.6\%.
21	Silver labels are produced by majority vote over three labeling functions; confidence equals the number of agreeing LFs (1--3).
22	Unless stated otherwise, evaluation uses the conf${\geq}$2 subset: $N{=}1{,}824$ for SWE-Agent (485 stagnation, 1,339 progress) and $N{=}43{,}376$ for OH.
23	
24	\begin{table}[t]
25	\centering
26	\small
27	\begin{tabular}{llrrc}
28	\toprule
29	\textbf{Agent} & \textbf{Source} & \textbf{Windows} & \textbf{Stag\,\%} & \textbf{Conf${\geq}$2} \\
30	\midrule
31	SWE-Agent & SWE-bench & 54,809 & 28.5 & 15,401 \\
32	OpenHands & CodeAct   & 150,652 & 6.6 & 43,376 \\
33	\bottomrule
34	\end{tabular}
35	\caption{Dataset statistics. Stagnation ratios differ substantially across agents, reflecting different action distributions.}
36	\label{tab:dataset_stats}
37	\end{table}
38	
39	\paragraph{Detection methods.}
40	(1)~\textbf{Structural features}: 30 hand-crafted features (repetition rates, file operation counts, edit distances, output entropy) fed to Logistic Regression (LR), Random Forest (RF), and Gradient Boosting (GB).
41	(2)~\textbf{ProgressProbe}: Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B \citep{zhang2025qwen3embedding} embeddings (1024-dim) processed by a 2-layer GRU \citep{cho2014gru} with attention \citep{bahdanau2015attention} (hidden$=$256, dropout$=$0.1), early-stopped at epoch~3 with patience~5.
42	(3)~\textbf{Mean-pool + LR}: Mean-pooled Qwen3 embeddings with logistic regression.
43	(4)~\textbf{LLM-as-Judge}: Claude Sonnet 4.6 zero-shot window-level classification (\$11.66 API cost for the SWE test set).
44	(5)~\textbf{Cosine similarity}: Cosine distance between consecutive window embeddings with a validation-tuned threshold.
45	
46	\paragraph{Metrics.}
47	Macro-F1 is the primary metric. We also report per-class F1 for stagnation (F1\textsubscript{stag}) and progress (F1\textsubscript{prog}).
48	
49	%-------------------------------------------------------------------
50	\subsection{Main Results}
51	\label{sec:main_results}
52	
53	Table~\ref{tab:main_results} presents in-domain results on the SWE-Agent conf${\geq}$2 test set and cross-agent transfer to OpenHands.

Best in \textbf{bold}, second-best \underline{underlined}.}
75	\label{tab:main_results}

77	
78	In-domain, structural RF achieves 0.9951 macro-F1, exceeding the GRU probe by 8.96 percentage points (pp) and the LLM judge by 33.3\,pp.
79	However, the structural--probe gap is inflated by circular evaluation: structural features reconstruct the LFs that generated the labels.
80	The more informative comparison is among non-circular methods: the GRU probe outperforms mean-pool~+~LR by 6.2\,pp, confirming that temporal modeling within windows adds value beyond static embedding aggregation.
81	The LLM judge underperforms all learned methods despite substantially higher cost.
82	
83	%-------------------------------------------------------------------
84	\subsection{Cross-Agent Transfer}
85	\label{sec:cross_agent}
86	
87	Table~\ref{tab:main_results} (right columns) shows models trained on SWE-Agent and evaluated on OpenHands without any OH training data.
88	Structural GB transfers best, achieving 0.967 macro-F1 on all OH windows---21.6\,pp above the probe fine-tuned on 100\% of OH data (0.751).
89	RF drops to 0.912 on all-confidence OH data despite matching GB in-domain, suggesting GB's boosted ensemble is more robust to distributional shift.
90	Both structural models recover to $>$0.99 on conf${\geq}$2 OH windows, where label noise is lower.
91	
92	The probe's zero-shot transfer (0.530 on all windows, 0.528 on conf${\geq}$2) is near chance, and even full OH fine-tuning only reaches 0.751.
93	This asymmetry---structural features transfer naturally while learned embeddings do not---is a central empirical finding: stagnation manifests in action-level structure that generalizes across agents.
94	
95	\paragraph{Multi-seed stability.}
96	Structural RF: $0.9951{\pm}0.0000$ in-domain (3 seeds, zero variance); GB cross-agent: $0.9678{\pm}0.0015$.
97	The probe shows higher variance: $0.9185{\pm}0.0113$, though all seeds exceed 0.90.
98	
99	%-------------------------------------------------------------------
100	\subsection{Robustness Analysis}
101	\label{sec:robustness}
102	
103	\paragraph{Encoder ablation.}
104	Replacing Qwen3-0.6B with BGE-M3 \citep{chen2024bgem3} or E5-large-v2 \citep{wang2024e5} yields probe macro-F1 of 0.9413 and 0.9363, respectively (vs.\ 0.9055 for Qwen3).
105	All encoders exceed 0.90, indicating the probe's temporal architecture, not a specific encoder, drives performance. Full results appear in Appendix Table~\ref{tab:encoder_ablation}.
106	
107	\paragraph{Window size.}
108	$k{=}5$ is optimal (0.9309 macro-F1); $k{=}3$ drops 5.9\,pp and $k{=}7$ drops 1.8\,pp.
109	Shorter windows lack sufficient context; longer windows dilute signal by spanning both progress and stagnation phases.
110	The 0.9309 figure differs from the main table's 0.9055 because the window ablation uses a separate train/val/test split (seed~42, Qwen3-0.6B encoder) to enable controlled comparison across window sizes; cross-split variance accounts for the gap.
111	Details in Appendix Table~\ref{tab:window_ablation}.
112	
113	\paragraph{Data scaling.}
114	Figure~\ref{fig:data_scaling} compares data efficiency across methods.
115	Structural classifiers are extremely data-efficient: RF achieves 0.991 and GB 0.987 at just 10\% training data, fully saturating by 50\%.
116	The probe scales monotonically from 0.805 (10\%) to 0.906 (100\%) but has not plateaued---a 10.1\,pp drop that is roughly 20$\times$ the structural degradation (${\sim}$0.4--0.8\,pp).
117	This data efficiency further supports the structural signal thesis: the features capture patterns so regular that minimal training data suffices.
118	
119	\begin{figure}[t]
120	\centering
121	\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{../../figures/paper/fig_data_scaling.pdf}
122	\caption{Macro-F1 vs.\ training data fraction. Structural classifiers (RF, GB) saturate by 50\% data; the probe scales monotonically but remains 9\,pp below at 100\%.}
123	\label{fig:data_scaling}
124	\end{figure}
125	
126	%-------------------------------------------------------------------
127	\subsection{Labeling Function Temporal Dynamics}
128	\label{sec:lf_temporal}
129	
130	We analyze when each LF first fires relative to the onset of stagnation episodes (Table~\ref{tab:lf_temporal}, Figure~\ref{fig:lf_temporal}).
131	
132	\begin{table}[t]
133	\centering
134	\small
135	\begin{tabular}{lrrrr}

\section{Analysis}
\label{sec:analysis}

\subsection{Circular Evaluation and Its Implications}
\label{sec:circular}

The structural RF's 0.9951 macro-F1 (\S\ref{sec:main_results}) is a predictable consequence of feature--label overlap, not a detection achievement.
The 30 structural features include repetition ratios and file operation counts---the same signals $\lambda_1$ and $\lambda_2$ consume to produce silver labels.
This score therefore represents an upper bound on LF reverse-engineering fidelity.

Two evaluation settings break this circularity.
First, cross-agent transfer: GB trained on SWE-Agent LF distributions achieves 0.9674 macro-F1 on OpenHands, where LF firing patterns differ substantially (e.g., cmd\_rep votes stagnation on 92.2\% vs.\ 65.5\% of windows).
The model cannot memorize LF outputs when tested on a different agent's distribution.
Second, a human-annotated gold set (\S\ref{sec:gold_set}) will provide definitive non-circular ground truth.
Until then, all in-domain structural metrics should be interpreted as LF-agreement scores rather than detection accuracy.

\subsection{Why Temporal Label Models Fail}
\label{sec:why_tlm_fail}

Despite clear temporal structure in LF activations (\S\ref{sec:lf_temporal}), no temporal label model improves downstream detection over majority vote (\S\ref{sec:temporal_label_models}).
The root cause is low label conflict in the 3-LF regime: conf${\geq}$2 windows dominate the training set, leaving few ambiguous labels for temporal models to correct.

TWV targets only conf${=}1$ windows, flipping 14.1\% of their labels.
These flips introduce noise rather than corrections---downstream probe F1 drops by 2.57\,pp relative to MV-trained.
HMM overpredicts stagnation (29,176 vs.\ 25,633 progress windows), producing a distorted label distribution that degrades the probe to 0.6564.
Lag-HMM, despite explicitly modeling per-LF temporal offsets, tracks MV within 0.1\,pp---the offset information captured by individual LFs (\S\ref{sec:lf_temporal}) does not translate into better aggregation.

Three binary LFs produce at most $2^3{=}8$ voting patterns, yielding too little conflict for temporal models to exploit.
A richer LF set ($>$10 functions with higher disagreement rates) would be needed to create the ambiguity where temporal aggregation could add value \citep{ratner2017snorkel}.

\subsection{Error Analysis}
\label{sec:error_analysis}

We analyze errors of the ProgressProbe (GRU) on the SWE-Agent conf${\geq}$2 test set under the stagnation-positive convention (positive = stagnation throughout).
The model misclassifies 131 of 1,824 windows (7.2\% error rate): 85 false negatives (predicted progress, actual stagnation; 64.9\% of errors) and 46 false positives (predicted stagnation, actual progress; 35.1\%).

The recall bottleneck is the dominant failure mode: $P_\text{stag}{=}0.897$ vs.\ $R_\text{stag}{=}0.825$.
Missed stagnation windows (FN) are not borderline cases---the model assigns them a mean stagnation probability of only 0.078 (i.e., high progress confidence of 0.922), with 73\% receiving $>$0.9 progress probability.
These windows feature agents performing diverse edits and varied commands that mimic progress patterns while making no effective headway, constituting a systematic blind spot.
False positives arise when agents repeat specific command patterns during genuine progress.

LF conflict is a strong error predictor: 39.7\% of error windows have at least one LF disagreeing, compared to a 31\% base rate.
The cmd\_rep LF contributes the highest per-LF error rate (12.75\%).
Errors concentrate in trajectory midpoints (10.2\% error rate vs.\ 6.5\% at endpoints), where the boundary between exploration and stagnation is most ambiguous.
Error mass is also non-uniform across trajectories: the two highest-error trajectories account for 18.3\% of all misclassifications.

\subsection{Outcome Backpropagation as Distant Supervision}
\label{sec:ob_analysis}

Outcome backpropagation ($\lambda_3$) is a privileged signal that uses task outcome, unavailable at inference time.
A 3-seed split-isolated holdout removing $\lambda_3$ yields macro-F1 of $0.770{\pm}0.022$, a 7.7\,pp drop from the 3-LF baseline of 0.847.
$\lambda_3$ contributes 33.5\% of conf${\geq}$2 labels (5,158 of 15,401 windows).

However, $\lambda_3$ functions as a coverage expander rather than an independent corrector: across 43,402 windows where both 2-LF and 3-LF configurations produce labels, their agreement is 100\%.
$\lambda_3$ never flips a majority vote---it only promotes conf${=}1$ windows to conf${=}2$ by adding a third agreeing vote.
This suggests that additional real-time LFs targeting the same coverage gaps could replace the privileged outcome signal without sacrificing label quality.

\section{Conclusion}
\label{sec:conclusion}

We presented a systematic study of progress stagnation detection in LLM coding agents, comparing structural features, neural embedding probes, and LLM-as-judge approaches.
Three findings emerge.

First, stagnation signals are fundamentally structural.
Thirty lightweight features achieve 0.9951 in-domain and 0.9674 cross-agent macro-F1, surpassing neural probes (0.9055) and LLM judges (0.6625) by wide margins.
These features are also data-efficient, maintaining F1 above 0.987 with only 10\% of training data.

Second, labeling functions exhibit agent-specific temporal dynamics.
Command repetition leads stagnation onset by 1.87 steps on SWE-Agent but reverses on OpenHands, where its high false-positive rate corrupts silver labels---removing it improves fine-tuned probe F1 by 17.6\,pp.

Third, temporal label models fail to improve over majority vote.
Three temporal aggregation methods---TWV, HMM, and lag-aware HMM---all underperform majority vote, constrained by insufficient inter-LF conflict among three binary labeling functions.

Agent monitoring should therefore prioritize lightweight structural features ({<}5\,ms per window, no GPU) over embedding or LLM approaches.
The circular evaluation caveat applies to in-domain results; cross-agent transfer provides stronger validation.

Future work includes extending evaluation to non-software-engineering agent domains, online integration with early termination or strategy switching, scaling to {>}10 labeling functions to test whether temporal aggregation becomes useful, and validation against the pending 650-window gold set.

16	3. **Temporal Label Model: A Well-Motivated Negative Finding (D039 negative result)**: 标准 data programming（majority vote）在 agent trajectory 上违反 i.i.d. 假设——LFs 产生系统性时序动态，这 motivate 了 temporal label model（TLM）的开发。然而，三种 TLM 实现**均未能超越简单 MV**：(a) **TWV（时序加权投票）**：绝大多数 σ 下有害（twv-ablation）；唯一微弱正向的 σ=2 训练的下游分类器全面劣化（in-domain -4.9pp, cross-agent -21.7pp, conf≥2 -1.8pp）(structural-on-twv)；(b) **HMM-TLM**：stagnation class overpredict；(c) **Lag-aware HMM**：仅追平 MV（0.8936）。**结论**：在当前 3-LF、低冲突（conf≥2 一致率 95.1%）的 regime 下，temporal alignment 的收益被噪声引入抵消。TWV 改变的主要是低置信标签，但改变方向是错的。这是对 "i.i.d. violation → temporal model must help" 这一直觉的重要否定，为未来 temporal label model 研究提供了关键约束条件。

18	## Story Spine

21	
22	- **Existing approaches & gaps**: (a) Cycle detectors（CDCS+CDSA, SpecRA, TrajAD）捕获重复/异常但漏掉语义多样的停滞；(b) Process Reward Models — **AgentPRM (Xi et al., ACM Web 2026, arxiv 2511.08325)** 是最直接的竞争者：用 TD/GAE 训练 step-level PRM 评估 "promise and progress"，但需要 outcome labels + RL pipeline，是 training signal 而非 monitoring tool。另有 PRM framework (arxiv 2502.10325)、ToolPRMBench (arxiv 2601.12294)、trajectory-level reward modeling (arxiv 2604.08178)。PRM 方向在 2025-2026 非常拥挤，我们的差异：**不需要 outcome labels**、**window-level 捕获 temporal dynamics**、**monitoring 而非 training**；(c) Self-reflection（Reflexion, LATS, Tree of Thoughts）依赖被困模型的自我评估，且是 intervention 而非 monitoring；(d) RL value functions (CodeRL) 需要 reward shaping；(e) **Agent monitoring 新方向**："Monitoring LLM Agents for Sequentially Contextual Harm" (ICLR 2025 Workshop) 论证了 sequence-level monitoring 的必要性（单步分析不够）；"Reliable Weak-to-Strong Monitoring" (arxiv 2508.19461) 研究了弱模型监控强 agent，但关注 safety 而非 progress；(f) **Agent degradation benchmark**：SlopCodeBench (arxiv 2603.24755, 2026) 量化了 coding agent 在长期任务中的退化——structural erosion 在 77% 轨迹上升、verbosity 在 75.5% 上升——为我们的 problem motivation 提供了最新实证。

25

Despite these well-characterized temporal patterns motivating a temporal label model, three implementations (TWV, HMM, lag-aware HMM) all fail to improve over simple majority vote — with TWV labels actually degrading downstream classifiers by up to 21.7pp. Our results establish structural features as the default choice for zero-data agent monitoring deployment."
27	
28	## Venue Fit Risks
29	
30	- **EMNLP vs ICSE**: 核心 LFs 和数据 100% 来自 SE 领域。贴合 NLP venue 的策略：(a) weak supervision on sequential data 是通用方法论，适用于任何有时序结构的标注场景——data programming / Snorkel 出自 NLP 社区；(b) structural vs semantic signal 的发现对任何 agent monitoring 系统有指导意义；(c) circular evaluation 问题是 weak supervision 评估的通用挑战；(d) TLM negative finding 对 sequential label model 研究有方法论价值。
31	- **Reviewer lottery**: 遇到 SE-skeptical 的 NLP reviewer 可能被判 "more suitable for ICSE/FSE"——通过强化方法论洞见的跨域普适性和 LLM agent 社区的 NLP 属性来降低风险。
32	- **"Negative finding paper 不够 novel"**: 论文不是纯 negative finding——structural signal discovery (Claim 1) 是强正面结果；TLM negative finding (Claim 3) 附带详细 failure analysis 和对未来研究的约束条件。EMNLP 接受 analysis paper 和 well-motivated negative results。
33	- **vs PRMs（2025-2026 最拥挤的方向）**: Related Work 加专门小节。核心定位差异：PRM 需要 outcome labels + RL pipeline（昂贵），我们是 monitoring tool + weak supervision pipeline（轻量）；PRM 是 step-level training signal，我们是 window-level detection。
34	- **"Why not LLM-as-judge?"**: 已有 baseline 对比——structural approach <5ms inference vs LLM 高开销，且 structural +24.3pp。
35	
36	## Anticipated Reviewer Concerns & Countermeasures
37	
38	| Concern | 应对 |
39	|---------|------|
40	| Circular evaluation（训练和评估都在自动标签上） | 多层防御：(1) 明确声明 F1 = LF consensus fidelity；(2) structural baseline 0.9951 量化 circularity 上界（逆向工程 LF 规则）；(3) Cross-domain OH 是 non-circular 评估；(4) **Gold set 人工标注**（650 窗口，关键路径） |
41	| Structural features outperform everything — so what's the point of the probe? | 论文已更新：probe 在 50% FT 后追平 structural（0.968 ≈ 0.967）。Probe 的价值：(1) 有目标域数据时性能收敛且支持 real-time inference + end-to-end deployment；(2) data scaling 曲线（0.598→0.968）展示真实学习过程，对比 structural 的 circular eval；(3) Gold set 上的对比是最终裁判 |
42	| Probe catches up with fine-tuning — is structural advantage real? | 零样本优势 +36.9pp 是真实且巨大的实用价值——部署时目标 agent 数据通常不可用。收敛现象本身是重要发现：stagnation 信号同时存在于结构和语义表示中，差异在于提取成本（structural = 零适配，probe = 需要域适配数据）。论文定位为 data efficiency advantage for deployment，不是 fundamental signal type difference |
43	| TLM negative finding 不够有 contribution | Failure analysis 详细到足以约束未来研究：(1) 3-LF 低冲突 regime（conf≥2 一致率 95.1%）限制了 temporal alignment 的改进空间；(2) TWV 在低置信区改变标签方向错误；(3) 三种不同实现排除了实现偏差。论文同时有强正面结果（Claim 1, 2） |
44	| 跨 agent 迁移只测了两个 SE agent | Two-agent scope 在 Limitations 讨论 + structural features 跨域 0.967 的强迁移证据。Future work 包含 non-SE agents |
45	| 为什么不直接用 LLM | LLM-as-judge baseline 已对比：structural RF +33.3pp、probe +24.3pp vs LLM、<5ms vs LLM 高开销 |
46	| outcome_backpropagation 信息泄露 | 3-seed holdout：移除 OB 后 f1_stag=0.641±0.034（-22pp），7.1pp 为纯信号贡献。OB 作为 "Privileged Distant Supervision"，在 3-LF 框架中不可替代 |
47	| Probe 只学了 LF 启发式 | LF oracle baseline（All-Agreement 0.854, probe +5.1pp）+ 错误分析（FP 65% = LF 未覆盖的语义多样停滞）+ gold set 最终验证 |
48	| Architecture novelty 不足 | 论文定位为 empirical analysis paper，novelty 在发现和方法论洞见，不在架构 |
49	| "Semantic stagnation" rebrands existing concepts | 明确映射到现有 agent failure mode taxonomy + window-level formulation 的特殊性论证 |
50	| Related work incomplete | 扩展到 30+ references：PRMs / agent self-reflection / weak supervision / agent degradation benchmarks |
51	| Embedding model unspecified | 具名 Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B + encoder ablation（BGE/E5/GTE，三者均 >0.90） |

53	| Structural data scaling 不能表述为 "robustness to data scarcity" | Circular eval 框架下正确解读：结构特征 ≈ LF 输入，10% 数据即可学会 LF→label 映射（RF 0.991）。这是 LF 重建的简单性证据，不是检测鲁棒性。论文呈现时标注 $^\dagger$ circular caveat，与 probe 的 data scaling（0.805→0.906，真正的学习曲线）对比呈现 |

3. **Temporal Label Model: A Well-Motivated Negative Finding (D039 negative result)**: 标准 data programming（majority vote）在 agent trajectory 上违反 i.i.d. 假设——LFs 产生系统性时序动态，这 motivate 了 temporal label model（TLM）的开发。然而，三种 TLM 实现**均未能超越简单 MV**：(a) **TWV（时序加权投票）**：绝大多数 σ 下有害（twv-ablation）；唯一微弱正向的 σ=2 训练的下游分类器全面劣化（in-domain -4.9pp, cross-agent -21.7pp, conf≥2 -1.8pp）(structural-on-twv)；(b) **HMM-TLM**：stagnation class overpredict；(c) **Lag-aware HMM**：仅追平 MV（0.8936）。**结论**：在当前 3-LF、低冲突（conf≥2 一致率 95.1%）的 regime 下，temporal alignment 的收益被噪声引入抵消。TWV 改变的主要是低置信标签，但改变方向是错的。这是对 "i.i.d. violation → temporal model must help" 这一直觉的重要否定，为未来 temporal label model 研究提供了关键约束条件。

## Story Spine

- **Problem**: LLM agents 在长期任务中频繁"语义停滞"——执行看似合理但集体无效的动作序列。每个动作可能非重复、局部合理，但整个窗口缺乏 goal-directed progress。现有方法要么检测结构性循环（漏掉语义多样的停滞），要么做 step-level scoring（丢失窗口内的时序动态），要么依赖 LLM 自我评估（高开销 + 受困模型的判断力受限）。

- **Existing approaches & gaps**: (a) Cycle detectors（CDCS+CDSA, SpecRA, TrajAD）捕获重复/异常但漏掉语义多样的停滞；(b) Process Reward Models — **AgentPRM (Xi et al., ACM Web 2026, arxiv 2511.08325)** 是最直接的竞争者：用 TD/GAE 训练 step-level PRM 评估 "promise and progress"，但需要 outcome labels + RL pipeline，是 training signal 而非 monitoring tool。另有 PRM framework (arxiv 2502.10325)、ToolPRMBench (arxiv 2601.12294)、trajectory-level reward modeling (arxiv 2604.08178)。PRM 方向在 2025-2026 非常拥挤，我们的差异：**不需要 outcome labels**、**window-level 捕获 temporal dynamics**、**monitoring 而非 training**；(c) Self-reflection（Reflexion, LATS, Tree of Thoughts）依赖被困模型的自我评估，且是 intervention 而非 monitoring；(d) RL value functions (CodeRL) 需要 reward shaping；(e) **Agent monitoring 新方向**："Monitoring LLM Agents for Sequentially Contextual Harm" (ICLR 2025 Workshop) 论证了 sequence-level monitoring 的必要性（单步分析不够）；"Reliable Weak-to-Strong Monitoring" (arxiv 2508.19461) 研究了弱模型监控强 agent，但关注 safety 而非 progress；(f) **Agent degradation benchmark**：SlopCodeBench (arxiv 2603.24755, 2026) 量化了 coding agent 在长期任务中的退化——structural erosion 在 77% 轨迹上升、verbosity 在 75.5% 上升——为我们的 problem motivation 提供了最新实证。

- **Our framing (D039 Pivot)**: Progress stagnation detection 的系统性实证研究。**三层贡献**：(1) **Zero-Shot Transfer Dominance (primary)** — 结构特征在零样本跨 agent 迁移上大幅领先 probe（+36.9pp）和 LLM-as-judge（+24.3pp），但 probe 在 ≤20% 目标域数据微调后缩至 2pp 内——结构特征是零数据部署的默认选择，有标注数据时两种方法收敛；(2) **LF Temporal Dynamics Analysis** — 量化 LFs 在 agent trajectory 上的时序角色 + 跨 agent 迁移分析 + circular evaluation 问题的方法论贡献——为 sequential data 上的 weak supervision 提供实证指导；(3) **TLM Negative Finding** — 系统性测试三种 temporal label model 实现，均未超越 MV，提供重要的负面结果和 failure analysis——约束未来研究方向。

- **Headline result template**: "We present a systematic empirical study of progress stagnation detection in LLM agents through weak supervision. Our central finding is that structural features dominate zero-shot cross-agent transfer: simple features (command repetition ratio, file diff frequency) achieve 0.995 in-domain and 0.967 cross-agent F1 with no target domain data, outperforming a zero-shot neural probe by 36.9pp and LLM-as-judge by 24.3pp. However, the probe rapidly closes this gap with modest fine-tuning — reaching within 2pp at 20% target data and matching structural performance at 50% — revealing that stagnation signals exist in both structural and semantic representations, but structural features transfer without adaptation. We further discover that labeling functions exhibit systematic but agent-specific temporal dynamics — command_repetition leads stagnation onset by ~1.87 steps on SWE-Agent but lags on OpenHands (+3.32 steps). A label quality audit reveals that fixing OH label version bias improves 5% fine-tuning from 0.570 to 0.850, demonstrating label quality as the dominant transfer bottleneck; prevalence-matched ablation shows cmd_rep's core value is coverage (-29.4pp when removed, p≈0), not label precision. Despite these well-characterized temporal patterns motivating a temporal label model, three implementations (TWV, HMM, lag-aware HMM) all fail to improve over simple majority vote — with TWV labels actually degrading downstream classifiers by up to 21.7pp. Our results establish structural features as the default choice for zero-data agent monitoring deployment."

## Venue Fit Risks

- **EMNLP vs ICSE**: 核心 LFs 和数据 100% 来自 SE 领域。贴合 NLP venue 的策略：(a) weak supervision on sequential data 是通用方法论，适用于任何有时序结构的标注场景——data programming / Snorkel 出自 NLP 社区；(b) structural vs semantic signal 的发现对任何 agent monitoring 系统有指导意义；(c) circular evaluation 问题是 weak supervision 评估的通用挑战；(d) TLM negative finding 对 sequential label model 研究有方法论价值。
- **Reviewer lottery**: 遇到 SE-skeptical 的 NLP reviewer 可能被判 "more suitable for ICSE/FSE"——通过强化方法论洞见的跨域普适性和 LLM agent 社区的 NLP 属性来降低风险。
- **"Negative finding paper 不够 novel"**: 论文不是纯 negative finding——structural signal discovery (Claim 1) 是强正面结果；TLM negative finding (Claim 3) 附带详细 failure analysis 和对未来研究的约束条件。EMNLP 接受 analysis paper 和 well-motivated negative results。
- **vs PRMs（2025-2026 最拥挤的方向）**: Related Work 加专门小节。核心定位差异：PRM 需要 outcome labels + RL pipeline（昂贵），我们是 monitoring tool + weak supervision pipeline（轻量）；PRM 是 step-level training signal，我们是 window-level detection。
- **"Why not LLM-as-judge?"**: 已有 baseline 对比——structural approach <5ms inference vs LLM 高开销，且 structural +24.3pp。

## Anticipated Reviewer Concerns & Countermeasures

| Concern | 应对 |
|---------|------|
| Circular evaluation（训练和评估都在自动标签上） | 多层防御：(1) 明确声明 F1 = LF consensus fidelity；(2) structural baseline 0.9951 量化 circularity 上界（逆向工程 LF 规则）；(3) Cross-domain OH 是 non-circular 评估；(4) **Gold set 人工标注**（650 窗口，关键路径） |
| Structural features outperform everything — so what's the point of the probe? | 论文已更新：probe 在 50% FT 后追平 structural（0.968 ≈ 0.967）。Probe 的价值：(1) 有目标域数据时性能收敛且支持 real-time inference + end-to-end deployment；(2) data scaling 曲线（0.598→0.968）展示真实学习过程，对比 structural 的 circular eval；(3) Gold set 上的对比是最终裁判 |
| Probe catches up with fine-tuning — is structural advantage real? | 零样本优势 +36.9pp 是真实且巨大的实用价值——部署时目标 agent 数据通常不可用。收敛现象本身是重要发现：stagnation 信号同时存在于结构和语义表示中，差异在于提取成本（structural = 零适配，probe = 需要域适配数据）。论文定位为 data efficiency advantage for deployment，不是 fundamental signal type difference |
| TLM negative finding 不够有 contribution | Failure analysis 详细到足以约束未来研究：(1) 3-LF 低冲突 regime（conf≥2 一致率 95.1%）限制了 temporal alignment 的改进空间；(2) TWV 在低置信区改变标签方向错误；(3) 三种不同实现排除了实现偏差。论文同时有强正面结果（Claim 1, 2） |
| 跨 agent 迁移只测了两个 SE agent | Two-agent scope 在 Limitations 讨论 + structural features 跨域 0.967 的强迁移证据。Future work 包含 non-SE agents |
| 为什么不直接用 LLM | LLM-as-judge baseline 已对比：structural RF +33.3pp、probe +24.3pp vs LLM、<5ms vs LLM 高开销 |
| outcome_backpropagation 信息泄露 | 3-seed holdout：移除 OB 后 f1_stag=0.641±0.034（-22pp），7.1pp 为纯信号贡献。OB 作为 "Privileged Distant Supervision"，在 3-LF 框架中不可替代 |
| Probe 只学了 LF 启发式 | LF oracle baseline（All-Agreement 0.854, probe +5.1pp）+ 错误分析（FP 65% = LF 未覆盖的语义多样停滞）+ gold set 最终验证 |
| Architecture novelty 不足 | 论文定位为 empirical analysis paper，novelty 在发现和方法论洞见，不在架构 |
| "Semantic stagnation" rebrands existing concepts | 明确映射到现有 agent failure mode taxonomy + window-level formulation 的特殊性论证 |
| Related work incomplete | 扩展到 30+ references：PRMs / agent self-reflection / weak supervision / agent degradation benchmarks |
| Embedding model unspecified | 具名 Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B + encoder ablation（BGE/E5/GTE，三者均 >0.90） |
| LF hold-one-out ablation 解读 | **禁止 "去掉 X 后 F1 更高" 的 claim**（test set 偏移假象）。正确框架：覆盖率贡献 + 跨集泛化 + 标签一致性 |
| Structural data scaling 不能表述为 "robustness to data scarcity" | Circular eval 框架下正确解读：结构特征 ≈ LF 输入，10% 数据即可学会 LF→label 映射（RF 0.991）。这是 LF 重建的简单性证据，不是检测鲁棒性。论文呈现时标注 $^\dagger$ circular caveat，与 probe 的 data scaling（0.805→0.906，真正的学习曲线）对比呈现 |

No systematic study examines WHAT signals actually carry stagnation information"
      - "Insight: stagnation is fundamentally structural—command repetition rates, file diff patterns, and outcome trajectories predict it near-perfectly WITHOUT semantic understanding. This overturns the intuition that detecting subtle agent failures requires sophisticated language understanding"
